does: Shaves the sharp corners from cut pieces of a firm vegetable, so that they hold their shape and do not break or cloud the liquid while they simmer.

intro.what: Sharp corners are shaved from firm vegetable pieces before simmering.
intro.why: Corners can break away in liquid. Rounding them helps the pieces retain their outline and keeps fragments from clouding the broth.

how: Hold a chunk in one hand and run a knife around its sharp edges, taking off a thin sliver from each corner.
Work around every chunk, so that all the corners are rounded.
Rinse the pieces, if they are starchy, before they go into the pot.

cues.text: The pieces have smooth, rounded corners and no sharp edges.
The pieces are smooth in the hand and do not catch.

mistakes.mistake: Taking off too much, which wastes the vegetable.
mistakes.fix: Take off only a thin sliver.

mistakes.mistake: Skipping it for long simmering, so that the corners break off and cloud the liquid.
mistakes.fix: Bevel the edges of any piece that will simmer for long.

quiz.question: Why round the corners of these vegetable pieces?
choices: To make every piece soften into the liquid.
To limit corners breaking into the simmering liquid.
To expose a larger rough face on each piece.
quiz.because: Removing vulnerable corners helps the pieces hold their shape and reduces loose fragments.

quiz.question: Where should the knife remove vegetable?
choices: Across the entire centre of each piece.
Deep into the broad flat faces.
Along the sharp corners, shaving lightly.
quiz.because: The aim is to round the corners while retaining the body of the cut piece.

quiz.question: What should a bevelled piece look like?
choices: A chunk with smooth rounded corners.
A much smaller piece with most of its broad faces removed.
A jagged piece with sharp points.
quiz.because: Rounded corners show the vulnerable edges have been removed without carving away the whole piece.

quiz.question: Too much vegetable is being lost while beveling. What should change?
choices: Cut deeper into each flat face.
Keep trimming the broad faces as well as the corners.
quiz.because: Light shaving rounds the corners without unnecessary waste.

comes_after.why: The edges are bevelled after the food is cut into pieces.
